title: DARPA Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Justification — Phase 65 Quantum review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Quantum reporting pack. DARPA's 360-page FY2027 justification requests $5.039 billion and organizes the portfolio around research sciences, information and communications, tactical and space systems, electronics, biological technology, and a dedicated Making, Maintaining, Supply Chain and Logistics program element. It is the strongest document in the collection for seeing where research ambition is tied to budget structure.
key_findings: The FY2027 request totals $5.039 billion in discretionary RDT&E.
Making, Maintaining, Supply Chain and Logistics appears as a dedicated program element alongside information, electronics, biomedical, tactical, space, sensing, and command-and-control work.
The portfolio spans basic research through advanced systems, making transition and industrial capacity recurring dependencies rather than downstream afterthoughts.
why_it_matters: Which records separate quantum research and migration policy from standards, procurement, tested interoperability, accepted cutover, and retired cryptography? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The budget book shows that logistics, production, sustainment, and supply-chain resilience are being treated as research objects alongside frontier technical capability.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking federal R&D as a dependency stack from discovery to production and sustainment.
Provides a primary-source baseline for DARPA funding direction before awards or technical outcomes are known.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
A budget request is not an enacted appropriation or an award record.
Program-element funding does not prove technical success, transition, procurement, or deployment.
